charts.title: Historical national accounts estimates of the share of the world's population living on less than $5 per day, by region

metadata.domain_context: Average incomes measured in national accounts are often much higher than those observed in survey data. See Roser and Hasell (2021) for further discussion.

charts.title: Winter temperature anomalies

metadata.domain_context: The difference between a month's average surface temperature from the mean temperature of the same month during the period 1991-2020, measured in degrees Celsius.

charts.title: Ocean acidification: mean seawater pH

metadata.domain_context: Mean seawater pH is shown based on in-situ measurements of pH from the Aloha station in Hawaii.

charts.title: Annual death rates at different ages in females

metadata.domain_context: The annual death rate, per 1,000 people of a given age. This is shown for females.

charts.title: Violent crime rates in the United States

metadata.domain_context: Estimated rates per 100,000 people. Violent crime includes four offenses: murder and non-negligent manslaughter, rape, robbery, and aggravated assault. Data for rape is not shown due to the lack of comparable data over time.

charts.title: Key features of women's political empowerment

metadata.domain_context: The indices are by V-Dem, based on expert estimates, and range from 0 to 1 (most empowered).

charts.title: Industry as a share of GDP vs. GDP per capita

metadata.domain_context: The vertical axis shows historical estimates of the share of industry in GDP. The horizontal axis shows GDP per capita, adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

charts.title: Sex ratio at birth vs. at five years old

metadata.domain_context: Sex ratio at birth, measured as the number of male births per 100 female births versus the sex ratio at five years old, measured as the number of males per 100 females. The grey line represents the point of equal ratio: countries which lie above this line had a higher sex ratio at birth than at five years old.

charts.title: Number of states involved in state-based conflicts

metadata.domain_context: Included are states that were primary participants in at least one interstate, intrastate, or extrasystemic conflict that was ongoing that year.

charts.title: Urban and rural population projected to 2050

metadata.domain_context: Number of people living in urban and rural areas, combining UN estimates and projections with modelled historical data back to 10,000 BCE.

charts.title: Malaria deaths by world region

metadata.domain_context: Estimated annual number of deaths from malaria across all ages and both sexes.

charts.title: Lighting sources in the United Kingdom

metadata.domain_context: The share of lighting across the United Kingdom, sourced from different energy sources.

charts.title: Perceived trust between people

metadata.domain_context: Share of answers to the question "How many people in this country trust one another?"

charts.title: Global sulphur dioxide (SO₂) emissions by world region

metadata.domain_context: Measured in tonnes per year.

charts.title: Countries that are long-standing full democracies

metadata.domain_context: Data by the Lexical Index of Electoral Democracy. Full democracies are political systems in which citizens have the right to choose the chief executive and the legislature in multi-party, uncertain elections, and enjoy freedoms of expression, assembly, and association.

charts.title: Monthly sea ice extent in the Antarctic

metadata.domain_context: Each point represents the monthly average sea ice extent. Years in the current decade are highlighted in red, with the current year highlighted in black.

charts.title: Learning-adjusted years of schooling vs. Electoral Democracy Index

metadata.domain_context: Learning-adjusted years of schooling merge the quantity and quality of education into one metric, accounting for the fact that similar durations of schooling can yield different learning outcomes. The electoral democracy index is by V-Dem, based on expert estimates, and ranges from 0 to 1 (most democratic).

charts.title: Net electricity imports as a share of electricity demand

metadata.domain_context: Net electricity imports are calculated as electricity imports minus exports. This is given as a share of a country's electricity demand. Countries with positive values are net importers of electricity; negative values are net exporters.

charts.title: COVID-19: Countries with restrictions on international travels

metadata.domain_context: Number of recorded countries with a given type of restriction on international travel arrivals.

charts.title: Survival ages across the population

metadata.domain_context: The number of years that a specific share of the population would survive, if they were born in a given year and experienced age-specific death rates of that year. For example, the line indicating 1% corresponds to the top 1% of survivors born in a given year and the number of years of their survival.

charts.title: Share of population living in multidimensional poverty

metadata.domain_context: Multidimensional poverty is defined as being deprived in a range of health, education and living standards indicators.

charts.title: Share of British adults who smoke cigarettes or use vapes/e-cigarettes

metadata.domain_context: An interactive visualization from Our World in Data.

charts.title: Deaths from protein-energy malnutrition, by age

metadata.domain_context: Estimated annual number of deaths from protein-energy malnutrition (which results from insufficient caloric and protein intake). Estimates come with wide uncertainties, especially for countries with poor vital registration.

charts.title: Fuel economy of new passenger vehicles

metadata.domain_context: Fuel economy is measured in liters per 100 kilometers traveled. This is shown as the average for new passenger vehicle registrations.

charts.title: Share of people who are undernourished vs. daily supply of calories

metadata.domain_context: Share of the total population with caloric intakes that fall below minimum energy requirements.

charts.title: Deaths from earthquakes

metadata.domain_context: Includes direct deaths from the event plus those from secondary impacts, such as a tsunami triggered by an earthquake. Due to data availability, recent data will be more complete than older historical estimates.

charts.title: Open defecation in rural areas vs. urban areas

metadata.domain_context: Open defecation refers to defecating in the open, such as in fields, forests, bushes, open bodies of water, on beaches, in other open spaces, or disposed of with solid waste.

charts.title: Mean adult height by year of birth, males vs. females

metadata.domain_context: Mean height for adult men versus adult women by year of birth i.e. data for 1996 is for men and women who were 18 years old in 2014.

charts.title: Global biomass vs. abundance of taxa

metadata.domain_context: Global biomass (measured in tonnes of carbon) versus the abundance (number of individuals) of different taxonomic groups. These are given as order-of-magnitude estimates.

charts.title: Opinions of young people on the threats of climate change

metadata.domain_context: Share of young people in each surveyed country that responded "yes" to each statement about climate change. 1,000 young people, aged 16 to 25 years old, were surveyed in each country.

charts.title: CO₂ reductions needed to keep global temperature rise below 1.5°C

metadata.domain_context: Annual emissions of carbon dioxide under various mitigation scenarios to keep global average temperature rise below 1.5°C. Scenarios are based on the CO₂ reductions necessary if mitigation had started – with global emissions peaking and quickly reducing – in the given year.

metadata.domain_context: Welfare cost is based on the quantity of years lived weighted by quality-of-life scores from detailed welfare assessments. A positive "welfare cost" is bad: it means there is a cost to animal welfare. A negative value indicates benefits to welfare.

metadata.alt_text: A stacked bar chart illustrating the distributions of categories on how parents with different infant feeding roles make use of digital technology to support their infant feeding practice. The category of technology use includes relating to the feeding experiences of others, assuring infant feeding practice, finding solutions to challenges in infant feeding and logging infant feeding practice. For the category of relating to the feeding experiences of others, 12.8% of breastfeeding parents responded neither agree nor disagree, 38.40% agreed, 36.80% strongly agreed. No bottle-feeding parents responded strongly disagree and disagree. 25.00% responded neither agree nor disagree, 41.67% responded agree, 33.33% responded strongly agree. 23.53% of partners responded responded neither agree nor disagree and 41.18% responded agree. For the assuring infant feeding practice category, 32.54% of breastfeeding parents responded agree while 34.92% responded strongly agree. 50% of bottle-feeding parents responded responded agree and 25.00% responded strongly agree. 23.53% of partners responded disagree, and 41.18% responded agree. For the finding solutions to challenges in infant feeding practice category, 37.7% of breastfeeding parents responded agree and 45.90% responded strongly agree. 33.33% of bottle-feeding parents responded agree and 33.33% responded strongly agree. 37.5% of partners responded agree, 31.25% responded strongly agree. For the logging infant feeding practice category, 34.92% of breastfeeding parents responded strongly disagree, and 25.40% responded strongly agree. 50% of bottle-feeding parents responded strongly agree. 31.25% of partners responded strongly disagree, and 31.25% responded strongly agree.
